title: Orthogonal session adapter and explainable retry profiles across SDKs
author: Sofia Morales
description:
Motivation: SDK teams have accumulated multiple slightly-different session/credential lifecycles and retry heuristics across Python, TypeScript and Go. This PR introduces an orthogonal 'session adapter' abstraction and a set of documented, explainable retry profiles that can be consumed uniformly by all three SDKs. Goals: 1) reduce surface area duplication across SDKs, 2) provide deterministic retry presets for common workload patterns, 3) improve streaming reauth ergonomics and observable retry behavior, and 4) bump SDK versions with backward-compatible adapters.

What this change does (single-string summary): Adds a lightweight SessionAdapter interface and a RetryProfile registry; implements adapters in python-sdk (session_adapter.py), ts-sdk (packages/connector/sessionAdapter.ts) and go-sdk (session/adapter.go); wires explainable retry presets (fast-interactive, bulk-throughput, safe-idempotent) into each SDK; updates streaming connectors to gracefully hand off refresh tokens during active pulls; and adds end-to-end tests and docs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc link: (internal) ENG-2345 session-adapter RFC
- [x] TypeScript implementation and tests
- [x] Python implementation and tests
- [x] Go implementation and tests
- [x] Telemetry hooks for retry-profile choice and session events
- [x] Migration guide in docs/ (backwards-compatible adapters exposed)
- [x] Version bumps: py 2.5.0, ts 1.9.0, go 1.12.0

Compatibility/migration notes: The SessionAdapter implements the existing TokenProvider surface but exposes a small opt-in shim: callers can pass a SessionAdapter instance where previously they passed a simple token supplier. If no adapter is provided, SDKs instantiate a default adapter that preserves current behavior. RetryProfile names are stable; teams can explicitly bind a profile to a client or rely on auto-selection heuristics.

Performance note: Benchmarks for typical conversational streaming workloads showed a 6-10% reduction in tail latency when adapters enable prefetching of refreshed tokens (warm handshake) and the fast-interactive RetryProfile is used. Bulk-throughput preserves batching behavior and keeps cost neutral.

Testing: Unit tests added per SDK, and an integration harness that runs a streaming handshake/reauth scenario with token rotation every 90s. A small fault-injection test validates that retry profiles emit expected decision traces.

Rollout plan: Gradual rollout with telemetry gating. Default adapter shipped; an opt-in feature flag controls auto-warm handshake in Hosted, to be enabled for 25% of traffic during the first week after merge.

Related: mirrors parts of ENG-2399 (retry telemetry) and addresses SUP-1024 (customer report: session drop during token rotation).

review_comments: Lina Chen (reviewer): Small request — can we expose the RetryProfile decision trace in telemetry with a stable key so metrics pipelines can correlate retries to client-observed latency?
Sofia Morales (author): Added telemetry tag 'sdk.retry_profile' and included decision_trace as a JSON blob (capped at 1KB) in the retry event. Updated docs to explain semantics.

George Patel (reviewer): In Go adapter, prefer explicit context propagation during prefetch; current implementation relies on background goroutines without cancellation. This caused a flaky test for me.
Sofia Morales (author): Switched to context-aware prefetch and added a unit test that cancels the context mid-prefetch; test is deterministic now.
Arjun Rao (reviewer): Approve after minor naming nit: rename fastInteractive -> fast-interactive for consistency with docs. Also request that release notes call out the opt-in flag.
Sofia Morales (author): Renamed profile and added release note entry about the opt-in handshake flag. Requesting final CI run.
merge_outcome: squash and merge; commit message preserved summary and linked Linear keys. Release branches: changes will be included in the next SDK maintenance release.
release_notes: Introduce SessionAdapter abstraction and three explainable RetryProfiles (fast-interactive, bulk-throughput, safe-idempotent). SDKs now support optional warm-handshake token prefetch for streaming connectors (opt-in via feature flag). SDK version bumps: python 2.5.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 1.12.0. Backwards-compatible adapters provided for smooth migration.
additional_notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: default behavior remains unchanged unless an adapter is supplied or the feature flag is enabled. Ops: enable telemetry gating to monitor retry_profile adoption and session-reuse metrics after rollout.
